title: True Worship
english: When a living creature is sacrificed upon it, the act is pious, not only because those who erected it and those who use it abstain from the slaughter of animals, but also because they, along with those who used it, were participants in piety, sharing in the altar’s piety, for having a living creature being sacrificed upon it is pious.
The fact that no animal was slaughtered on the altar of the pious, which was at Delos, demonstrates that God is not pleased with blood sacrifices, but rather with worship in spirit and truth.

Moses, a sincere servant of the divine words, is not a false speaker, and the law, which is written in letters, serves as a teacher of the foolish and a guide for infants, as Paul, who was educated in the law, explains.

According to Paul, we should use the elements and the principles of the disciplines to understand the truth, and to exercise ourselves in the types of truth, allowing us to be occupied with childish things for a time, for it was possible for the Israelites, who had a new spirit and truth, to fulfill their worship and service in spirit and truth, and to live a holy and pure life.
Virtue is not easily perfected, and a certain Greek poet has expressed the view that great things can be compared to small labors, whereas others may say that labor is comparable to small things.

However, the power of living well and the subtlety of doctrine would be a burden to the minds of the Jews, and the lawgiver himself teaches through the voice of Isaiah, saying, 'You do not know, you do not understand, you have not been opened from the beginning' (Isaiah 29:13).
For I knew that you would disobey, for you have been disobedient and rebellious (Isaiah 29:13).

When Moses received the law from God and was on the mountain, the Israelites turned to defection and dared to give divine honors to a calf, and they followed it, saying, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt' (Exodus 32:8).

It is questionable how they would have received evangelical discipline, so as to consecrate intellectual worship to God in place of spiritual sacrifice, and instead of the slaughter of animals, the fragrance of virtues, for they were immolating sheep, oxen, goats, and turtledoves, and also pigeons.

But it is necessary to see and admire the divine economy’s wonder, for when God permitted the Israelites to perform sacred rites in Egypt, they did so in a manner that was customary for them, and thus gradually taught them to offer perfect sacrifices, not in the usual manner, but rather wisely and spiritually.

A lamb was sacrificed in Egypt by the Israelites during the Passover festival, not simply, but wisely, and the tenth day of the first month was taken, and a lamb was slaughtered on the fourteenth day towards evening, as it was written: 'You will eat it with lamps, and your loins will be girded, and your sandals will be on your feet, and you will eat it with haste, for it is the Passover of the Lord' (Exodus 12:11).

In each of the sacrifices, there was a certain ritual, not established by men, but something was being foreshadowed in them, and now we must come to the point and demonstrate the legal cult, which is less pleasing to God, for we often hear through the voice of the prophets speaking clearly, saying, 'Who has required these things from your hands?' (Isaiah 29:13).
translator_notes: The text begins mid-sentence with '…With a living creature being sacrificed upon it'.
The source text is a fragment, with some sentences cut off mid-word or mid-sentence.
